clue.text: Strikebreaker returns to secure objective

indicators.note: returns tells us the word for a strikebreaker is read backwards

parts.note: a rat is slang for a strikebreaker or scab
to secure something is to get it

explanation.surface: A scab heads back to work to lock down some goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikebreaker' looks like part of a labour-dispute definition, but it is slang wordplay; 'objective' at the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal you aim at is a target, a synonym.

clue.text: Sound woman studied a snake

indicators.note: sound says the words for the woman, studied and a are heard as one word

parts.note: the woman Anna, conned for studied (to con is to study), then a

explanation.surface: A woman read up on a serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: A large South American constrictor is a type of snake.

clue.text: An expert in metabolic disease who can't settle down?

definitions.text: An expert in metabolic disease who can't settle down?

parts.words: An expert in metabolic disease who can't settle down?
parts.note: gout is a metabolic disease; really a restless rover

explanation.surface: A gout specialist who is always on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout is a pleasure-seeker always roaming from place to place.

clue.text: Paddy took food, eschewing alcohol

parts.note: a paddy is British slang for a fit of temper
ate is took food

explanation.surface: An Irishman had his meal without drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irishman's name; in British slang a paddy is a tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate can mean abstaining from drink, teetotal.

clue.text: Pitch constantly used by certain players

definitions.text: Pitch constantly used by certain players

parts.words: Pitch constantly used by certain players
parts.note: a single unvarying pitch, as in a dull speaker's voice, or the single-channel sound of some record players

explanation.surface: Some musicians keep to one note throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' suggests musicians but also hints at mono record players.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice or sound held at one unchanging pitch is described with this word.

clue.text: Spoilt son safe with two chums, very similar

indicators.note: spoilt means the letters given by the words after it are ruined into a new order
two means the word for a pal is used twice

parts.note: a chum is a friend; two of them give the letters twice

explanation.surface: A pampered boy feels secure with a pair of friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoilt' looks like describing the son but rearranges SONSAFE plus CHUMCHUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom meaning practically the same, with little to choose between.

clue.text: Unacceptable conflict takes duke away from port

parts.note: out means not acceptable, as in 'that's out'
war is conflict

explanation.surface: An unacceptable war removes a nobleman from a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes ... away' seems to signal a deletion; 'away from port' is the definition and 'takes' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship heading out of harbour is outward bound.

clue.text: It's satisfactory for its zip code

definitions.text: It's satisfactory for its zip code

parts.words: It's satisfactory for its zip code
parts.note: the US state whose two-letter postal code is OK, the abbreviation meaning satisfactory

explanation.surface: A place's postal code happens to be fine.
explanation.definitionFit: This US state's two-letter postal abbreviation is the same as 'okay'.

clue.text: Beneficiary's aim, to ensure gold is received

parts.note: an end is an aim
OR is gold in heraldry
to see to it is to ensure

explanation.surface: A recipient's goal is to make sure the gold arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: The person to whom a cheque is signed over is the one who benefits.

clue.text: Widespread complaint has US politician in a flap

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for the US politician inside the word for a flap

parts.note: to be in a flap is to be in a panic
DEM is short for a Democrat in American politics

explanation.surface: A grumble spreads while an American politician panics.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease spread across a whole region is a widespread illness, complaint meaning ailment.

clue.text: Dull part of trips to lido

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Outings to the swimming pool can be boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stolid is impassive and unexciting, hence dull.

clue.text: It may be felt necessary to protect head from sun

definitions.text: It may be felt necessary to protect head from sun

parts.words: It may be felt necessary to protect head from sun
parts.note: a wide-brimmed hat, often made of felt, worn against the sunshine

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a head covering is needed in strong sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'felt' reads as a verb (thought) but is the material the hat is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad-brimmed Mexican hat worn as a shield against the sun.

clue.text: Understand articles in Greek

indicators.note: in puts the two articles inside the abbreviation for Greek

parts.note: A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: Grasping grammatical articles in the Greek language.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather is to infer or understand from what one hears.

clue.text: End a tuba arrangement with no diminuendo?

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reorders the letters of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A tuba piece that ends without getting quieter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' suits the musical surface but signals an anagram of ENDATUBA.
explanation.definitionFit: Without lessening in force, as music with no diminuendo does not grow softer.

clue.text: Suite of ten pieces written before the twentieth century?

indicators.note: written before puts the broken-up letters first
pieces breaks the word ten into bits to be reassembled

parts.note: to a writer then, the twentieth century was our age

explanation.surface: A musical suite in ten movements composed before 1900.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suite' looks musical but means a retinue; 'pieces' scrambles TEN to ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A suite is a group of attendants, a retinue.

clue.text: Point about current treaty

indicators.note: about means the abbreviation for point goes around the one for current

parts.note: AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: Someone makes a point about an up-to-date agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: An agreement between parties is a pact, a synonym of treaty.

clue.text: Miserably inadequate male in quiet upper room

parts.note: P is piano, quiet in music

indicators.note: in puts the male pronoun inside the upper room

parts.note: an attic is a room at the top of a house
he is a male

explanation.surface: A man in a silent attic is in a sorry state.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pitifully feeble or useless is pathetic.

clue.text: Supercilious and ' laughing when put in the picture

definitions.text: laughing when put in the picture
definitions.meaning: Frans Hals's portrait The Laughing ... puts the man laughing in the picture

explanation.surface: Arrogant and amused once someone has been informed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in the picture' looks like 'informed' but refers to a famous painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Haughtily dismissive is the adjectival sense; a Royalist gentleman is the noun in Hals's painting.

clue.text: It's kept by a lookout in an underground hollow

definitions.meaning: in old British school slang a boy keeping watch 'kept ...', Latin for 'beware'
a hollow space beneath the ground, as in a hillside

explanation.surface: A lookout stands guard over a hole in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'keep cave' was British public-school slang for keeping watch for teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural chamber below ground is a cavern; the Latin warning word means beware.

clue.text: Coach-drivers initially hate dropping a gear

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the coach-drivers
dropping means the letter A is let go from the word for hate

parts.note: loathing is hatred

explanation.surface: Bus drivers loathe changing down a gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gear' looks mechanical but means garments; LOATHING less A gives LOTHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear can mean garments, as in sports gear.

clue.text: European citizens compete, gaining five points

parts.note: to vie is to compete
N, N, E, S and E are five compass points

explanation.surface: Citizens of Europe compete and pick up five points.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Austria's capital city are known by this name.

clue.text: Compensation left in old Spanish currency

indicators.note: in puts the word for left inside the old Spanish coin

parts.note: the real was an old Spanish coin
to have quit is to have left

explanation.surface: Damages paid out in former Spanish money.
explanation.definitionFit: Requital is repayment or recompense for something done.

clue.text: Sit near free wine

indicators.note: free means the letters of the words before it are set loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Sit by some complimentary drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Sailor's skill in country dance

indicators.note: in places the word for skill inside the country dance

parts.note: a hey is an old country dance
art means skill

explanation.surface: A seaman shows off his skill at a folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors are traditionally addressed as 'my hearties', so a shipmate is one.

clue.text: Poignant activity Scrooge experienced thrice

definitions.meaning: deeply moving and lingering in the memory
in Dickens's A Christmas Carol three spirits visit Scrooge, a ghostly visitation each time

explanation.surface: A touching account of what Scrooge went through three times.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune that lingers movingly is described so; ghosts visiting someone are doing this.

clue.text: Minutiae of civic centre shown in rejected painting

indicators.note: shown in puts the centre of civic inside the reversed word for painting
rejected sends the word for painting back the other way

parts.note: painting is art

indicators.note: centre takes the letters of civic without its first and last

explanation.surface: Small details of a town centre appear in a refused painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the painting word backwards to TRA, and 'centre' strips the outer letters from civic before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial details or small points are trifles, synonyms of minutiae.

clue.text: Judgmental type who has all the answers

definitions.text: Judgmental type who has all the answers

parts.words: Judgmental type who has all the answers
parts.note: a know-all seems meant, but it is the person marking a test, who holds the answer sheet and passes judgment

explanation.surface: A judgmental know-all who thinks they're always right.
explanation.definitionFit: The person setting and marking a test judges candidates and holds the correct responses.

clue.text: Theatre furnishings? They're the end!

definitions.meaning: the drapes hanging before a stage
slang for death or finish, as in 'it's all over for him'

explanation.definitionFit: Stage drapes close a show, and slang uses the same word for doom or the finish.

clue.text: Head off dog beginning to track young bird

indicators.note: head off means the first letter of the word for the dog is removed

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of dog

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of track

explanation.surface: A hound heads off to start following a fledgling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' drops B from BEAGLE, leaving EAGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chick of a large bird of prey is the young of the eagle.
